narrative.overview: Meridian treats the site as an official registry of the ground. The aesthetic currency is proof: DTCP approval stamps, spec ledgers with label-left/value-right rows, plot ledgers with status dots, and honest — placeholders where the client has not yet supplied a fact. Navy owns hierarchy; brass is spent like wax on a seal — only on actions and proof marks, never decoration. White instrument cards float on warm survey paper. The system reads institutional, not corporate-glossy. Photography is real site ground — soil, lawns, roads, signboards — because buyers buy land. Density alternates deliberately: full-bleed image moments against dense typographic ledgers, one message per hero.
keyCharacteristics: Navy hierarchy, brass scarcity, warm paper canvas
Single type family (Manrope) with tabular numerals on every figure
Ledger grammar: uppercase micro-labels opposite tabular values, separated by hairlines
Approval/verification as designed first-class elements (stamps, green badges), never footnotes
Unconfirmed facts render as — / marked * sample data — visible honesty as craft

rules.name: The Gold-Sparseness Rule
rules.body: Brass appears only on actions (buttons, CTAs) and proof marks (top rule of the stat band, eyebrow labels). If gold makes something prettier but not more actionable or more provable, remove it.

rules.name: The Green-Means-Verified Rule
rules.body: #1d6b45 is exclusively a verification signal — DTCP approval, plot availability. No green headings, no green decoration.

rules.name: The Honest-Placeholder Rule
rules.body: Unconfirmed facts render as — or marked * sample data with the .sample-flag ribbon. Never lorem, never invented numbers, never silent blanks.

rules.name: The Tabular Ledger Rule
rules.body: Every figure on the page uses tabular numerals. Stats, prices, plot numbers, availability counts — all align vertically.

rules.name: The Two-Step Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never a third shadow strength. Depth is response or floating chrome, never decoration — shadows don't pile up inside nested cards.

dos: Do use tabular numerals on every stat, price, and count.
Do reserve green for DTCP verification and availability only.
Do mark every unconfirmed figure with the * mark and .req class, with the sample-flag ribbon on the page.
Do show the ground — soil, lawns, roads, signboards — in photography.
Do keep the validated hero veil (.60/.24/.78 navy gradient) on photographic heroes.
Do use the 3px brass top rule to mark proof bands.
donts: Don't use brass/gold as decoration — actions and proof only (client-locked).
Don't print signboard approval numbers (e.g. No. 26/2016) as page text — they are visible in photos but unconfirmed.
Don't use real VSS site photos as full-bleed heroes (low-res camera shots); the only hero-grade image is the aerial concept render, never captioned as a specific project.
Don't invent facts, testimonials, statistics, prices, or approvals — render — instead.
Don't gradient-fill ghost numerals on project imagery — client explicitly rejected gold and glossy-white fills; keep transparent glyphs with the 1.5px white stroke.
Don't copy reference sites (Anehana, Hosachiguru, Kendrick Guehr, G Square) — borrow ideas, never look.
